report.source_text: Pathology from the upper endoscopy revealed rare gland abscesses and diffuse lamina propria neutrophilic inflammation. Rare eosinophils were found as well as small lymphoid aggregates of polymorphic small lymphocytes. Stains for CMV and H. pylori were negative (after having received about two weeks of H. pylori directed treatment). There was no evidence of lymphoma or other malignancy.

report.source_text: The patient received a 14-day course of IV daptomycin (due to a medication reaction, IV vancomycin was deferred) and cefepime. He also eventually completed a two-week course of quadruple therapy for Helicobacter pylori infection. He was followed closely by Infectious Disease, General Surgery, and Gastroenterology during his stay. Half-way through the antibiotic course for phlegmonous gastritis his symptoms began improving, his appetite returned, and radiographic thickening of the gastric lining resolved. Three months following his initial hospitalization he is now in his usual state of health and follow up upper endoscopy revealed normal gross appearance of his stomach and esophagus. He did not require gastrectomy nor other surgical management.
report.temporal_cue: during and three months after hospitalization

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 19-year-old man presented with three weeks of severe epigastric pain, non-bloody vomiting, and 15-pound weight loss following failed H. pylori eradication therapy. Initial workup revealed leukocytosis with left shift (14.90 x10^3 cells/uL) and elevated lipase (428 U/L). CT imaging demonstrated diffuse gastric wall thickening with mucosal enhancement, retained fluid, and diffuse mesenteric/gastrohepatic/para-aortic adenopathy without pancreatic enhancement. Upper endoscopy revealed severely inflamed, eroded, friable, nodular gastric mucosa and erythematous duodenal mucosa. Histopathology confirmed rare gland abscesses with diffuse lamina propria neutrophilic inflammation, negative CMV and H. pylori stains, and no malignancy. Gastric biopsy cultures grew Granulicatella adiacens, while blood cultures and extensive infectious workup (HIV, COVID-19, TB, CMV viremia) remained negative. The patient received 14 days of IV daptomycin and cefepime plus quadruple therapy for H. pylori, with symptomatic improvement mid-course and resolution of gastric wall thickening on imaging. Three-month follow-up endoscopy showed normal gastric and esophageal mucosa without need for surgical intervention.
